name: sqlserver-trap
request: Add stock. Add a table StockLevels (Sku varchar(32) primary key, Available int). POST /orders reserves the stock for each line: Available goes down and never below zero. When a line has not enough stock, POST /orders returns 409 and reserves nothing. Add PUT /stock/{sku} with the body {"available": 25}. The warehouse calls it to create or replace the level of a SKU, often twice at the same time for one SKU. Also add GET /reports/daily-sales?from=2026-07-01&to=2026-07-31. It returns one row per day in Amsterdam time, with the number of orders and the revenue (the sum of the line totals) of the orders that are not cancelled, as a JSON array: [{"day": "2026-07-02", "orders": 3, "revenue": 12.50}]. The report runs during the day and must not block order placement. Add the EF Core migration.
traps: Read the stock, check it in C#, then write: oversell under parallel orders. Use one conditional UPDATE (or ExecuteUpdateAsync) per line and check the row count.
Check-then-insert, or MERGE without HOLDLOCK, for the upsert: error 2627 when two calls insert the same new SKU.
AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Amsterdam': SQL Server takes only Windows zone names (error 9820). Use 'W. Europe Standard Time'.
NOLOCK or READ UNCOMMITTED in the report to avoid blocking. The fix is RCSI on the database (DATA-26).
The fixture turns on EnableRetryOnFailure: an explicit transaction outside the execution strategy throws InvalidOperationException.
Raw SQL with an interpolated string on the varchar(32) key sends nvarchar(4000): the index cannot seek.

assertions.trap: Oversell, 2627 on a parallel upsert, IANA zone name, transaction outside the execution strategy.
NOLOCK or READ UNCOMMITTED in the report.

assertions.judge: The final message proposes READ_COMMITTED_SNAPSHOT (RCSI, DATA-26) for the report instead of a lock hint, and marks it as an assumed decision or an open point for the DBA. A migration that turns RCSI on also passes when it runs outside a transaction (suppressTransaction) and the message names the effect.

The reservation is one atomic statement per SKU (UPDATE ... WHERE Sku = @sku AND Available >= @q, or ExecuteUpdateAsync with the same Where) with a check of the row count, inside one transaction that runs inside the execution strategy (CreateExecutionStrategy().ExecuteAsync). A tracked read, a check in C#, and SaveChanges does not pass, also not with a rowversion token and no retry.

Raw SQL that filters on Sku uses LINQ, a SqlParameter with SqlDbType.VarChar and size 32, or explains the nvarchar conversion. An interpolated C# string in SqlQuery or ExecuteSql on the Sku column without this does not pass.
The final message states the assumptions with the chosen answers: at least the time zone name, the RCSI or isolation choice, and how the migration is deployed.

name: sqlserver-review
request: Review this code before we merge it. It connects the orders service to the stock in the SQL Server database of the warehouse team: a Dapper repository and the procedures and schema script for that database.

assertions.judge: The review finds at least 6 of the 8 planted mistakes.
The review finds every planted mistake with severity 'high'.

At most 2 findings are false positives. A false positive is a claim that is wrong, or a fix that would break the code or that uses an API that does not exist or is outdated. A real problem that is not on the planted list is not a false positive.
Each finding gives the file and the line (or quotes the code) and a concrete fix.
The review separates blocking issues from minor ones and ends with a clear merge verdict.

The fixes are correct for SQL Server 2025: 'W. Europe Standard Time' (a Windows zone name) for AT TIME ZONE, MERGE WITH (HOLDLOCK) or UPDLOCK plus HOLDLOCK for the upsert, sp_executesql with parameters and QUOTENAME for the dynamic sort, RCSI instead of NOLOCK, and a VarChar parameter with size 32 instead of AddWithValue. The review respects DATA-29 (the warehouse procedures are accepted) and does not ask to move them into C#.
